title: “We do use it, but not how hearing people think”: How the Deaf and Hard of Hearing Community Uses Large Language Model Tools

bias_targets.methodology: A mixed-methods approach utilizing an online survey of 80 Deaf and Hard of Hearing (DHH) individuals and semi-structured, task-based interviews with 11 DHH participants to evaluate model limitations in understanding deafness, including analyzing how AI models define historically sensitive terminology (e.g., the word 'dumb').

Thematic analysis of user survey and interview responses to identify the models' lack of support for American Sign Language (ASL) grammar/gloss, their reliance on high English proficiency, and the models' default adherence to 'hearing culture' communication norms.
